Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

# Labour Party Manifesto 2024: Summary

## Core Priorities

The manifesto establishes five national missions: economic growth, clean energy, crime reduction, breaking barriers to opportunity, and NHS reform.

## Economic Policy

Labour commits to fiscal rules requiring balanced day-to-day budgets and falling debt by the fifth forecast year. Corporation tax will be capped at 25%. The party proposes a National Wealth Fund (£7.3 billion) to attract private investment, an Industrial Strategy Council, and business rates reform. Planning system changes aim to deliver 1.5 million new homes. A "New Deal for Working People" includes banning zero-hours contracts, ending fire-and-rehire practices, and raising minimum wage to a living wage.

## Energy and Environment

Great British Energy, a publicly-owned company headquartered in Scotland, will receive £8.3 billion. Targets include zero-carbon electricity by 2030 through expanded wind, solar, and nuclear power. No new oil/gas exploration licences will be issued, though existing operations continue. The Warm Homes Plan allocates £6.6 billion for home energy upgrades.

## Public Services

NHS reforms include 40,000 additional weekly appointments, doubled CT/MRI scanners, and 8,500 new mental health staff. Dentistry receives 700,000 urgent appointments. Social care moves toward a National Care Service with national standards.

Education proposals include 6,500 new teachers funded by ending private school tax exemptions, free primary school breakfast clubs, and curriculum review. Skills England will oversee a reformed apprenticeship levy.

## Crime and Justice

Plans include neighbourhood policing guarantees, Respect Orders for antisocial behaviour, knife crime reduction through intervention programmes, and halving violence against women within a decade. Specialist rape courts and domestic abuse experts in emergency services are proposed.

## Immigration and Borders

A Border Security Command will replace the Rwanda scheme, using counter-terrorism powers against smuggling gangs. Additional caseworkers will clear asylum backlogs, and a returns unit will expedite removals.

## Constitutional Reform

Hereditary peers will lose voting rights, with mandatory retirement at 80 for Lords members. Voting age drops to 16. An Ethics and Integrity Commission will oversee ministerial standards.

## Foreign Policy

NATO commitment remains central, with a Strategic Defence Review planned. The party seeks improved EU relations through veterinary agreements and security cooperation without rejoining single market or customs union. Support for Ukraine continues, including backing NATO membership pathways.

## Devolution

Enhanced powers for Combined Authorities and mayors, with Local Growth Plans required. Relationships with Scottish, Welsh, and Northern Ireland governments will be reset through a Council of Nations and Regions.
